uphold.cite: Roa v. Lodi Medical Group, Inc., 37 Cal.3d 920 (1985)
uphold.rule: §6146 constitutional; fee agreements exceeding §6146 are voidable by client regardless of written agreement

sirva_fee_calculation.note: This is an attractive case for plaintiff's malpractice firms under the AB 35 fee schedule.

spine_surgery_intentional_tort.hrimnak_escape: Framing as fraud/battery removes the case from MICRA's professional negligence scope — §6146 does NOT apply to intentional tort claims. Standard contingency rules govern. Attorney may negotiate 33%–40% standard contingency.
spine_surgery_intentional_tort.note: The §6146 limitation is MICRA-specific. Intentional tort claims are not 'medical malpractice' for fee-cap purposes.

operational_notes_for_steward_cases.pro_se_note: §6146 governs attorney-client contingency fee agreements. Michael acting pro se has no attorney fee to calculate — he retains 100% of any recovery. §6146 only becomes relevant when engaging malpractice counsel.
operational_notes_for_steward_cases.disclosure_checklist: When retaining malpractice attorney: (1) Receive written §6146 fee schedule disclosure; (2) Verify fee agreement does not exceed statutory maximums; (3) Clarify whether attorney will advance litigation costs (affects net vs. gross recovery calculation for fee base); (4) Obtain written confirmation that the Hrimnak/intentional tort framing is being pursued for spine surgery case (takes case outside §6146)
